idiomatic: Yao Prefecture (cishi).

literal: Originally Bohai Jiao Prefecture; former counties five: Jiaoshan, Diaoling, Siquan, Jianshan, and Yanyuan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Jiao Prefecture; five former counties—Jiaoshan, Diaoling, Siquan, Jianshan, Yanyuan—all abolished.
700 households.
Under Hai Prefecture.

literal: Two hundred li northeast of Hai Prefecture.
idiomatic: Hai Prefecture lay two hundred li to the northeast.
One county:
Yanyuan County.

literal: East borders Silla; the old Pyongyang city lies southwest of the county.
idiomatic: It bordered Silla on the east; old Pyongyang lay southwest of the county.

literal: One hundred twenty li northeast of Hai Prefecture.
idiomatic: One hundred twenty li northeast of Hai.
Pin Prefecture (Rouyuan Army), cishi.

literal: Originally Bohai Qing Prefecture; former counties five: Tianqing, Shenyang, Lianchi, Langshan, and Xianyan—all abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Qing Prefecture; five former counties—Tianqing, Shenyang, Lianchi, Langshan, Xianyan—all abolished.
500 households.
Under Hai Prefecture.

literal: One hundred twenty li southeast of Hai Prefecture.
idiomatic: One hundred twenty li southeast of Hai.

literal: Lu Prefecture, Yalu Army, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Lu Prefecture (Yalu Army), military commissioner.

literal: Originally old Goryeo state; Bohai styled it Western Capital Yalu Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally core Goryeo territory; Bohai called it Western Capital Yalu Prefecture.

literal: Walls three zhang high, twenty li in circuit; it superintended Shen, Huan, Feng, and Zheng four prefectures.
idiomatic: Walls three zhang high, twenty li around; it oversaw Shen, Huan, Feng, and Zheng prefectures.

literal: Former counties three: Shenlu, Shenhua, and Jianmen—all abolished.
idiomatic: Three former counties—Shenlu, Shenhua, Jianmen—all abolished.

literal: When Da Yanlin rebelled, remnant factions were moved to Shangjing and Yisu County established for them.
idiomatic: Da Yanlin's rebellion sent survivors to Shangjing and founded Yisu County for them.
2,000 households remained.

literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital regent office.
idiomatic: Under the Eastern Capital regent office.

literal: Governing four prefectures and two counties:
idiomatic: Four prefectures, two counties:
Hongwen County.
Shenxiang County.
Huan Prefecture.

literal: Goryeo central capital city; former counties three: Huandu, Shenxiang, and Qi River—10 all abolished.
idiomatic: Goryeo's central capital; three former counties—Huandu, Shenxiang, Qi River—tenth note: all abolished.

literal: The Goryeo king here built palaces; the people called it the New State.
idiomatic: A Goryeo king raised palaces here; subjects called it the New State.

literal: Five generations later Zhao, at Jin Emperor Kangdi's Jianyuan opening, was defeated by Murong and the palaces burned.
idiomatic: Five generations on, Zhao was crushed by Murong at Jin Kangdi's Jianyuan opening and the palaces burned.
700 households.
Under Lu Prefecture.
Two hundred li to the southwest.
Feng Prefecture.

literal: Bohai established Pan'an Commandery; former counties four: Anfeng, Boke, Xirang, and Xiashi—all abolished.
idiomatic: Bohai's Pan'an Commandery had four former counties—Anfeng, Boke, Xirang, Xiashi—all abolished.
300 households.
Under Lu Prefecture.
Two hundred ten li to the northeast.
Zheng Prefecture.

literal: Originally Beiru King's land; the state was annexed by Gongsun Kang.
idiomatic: Originally the Beiru king's domain, later annexed by Gongsun Kang.
Bohai founded Beiru Commandery.
The Beiru River ran through it.
500 households.
Under Lu Prefecture.
Three hundred eighty li to the northwest.
One county:
Dongna County.
Originally Han Dongnai County territory.

literal: 11 Seventy li west of the prefecture.
idiomatic: Eleventh note: seventy li west of the prefecture.
Mu Prefecture.

literal: Originally Bohai Anyuan Prefecture land; former counties two: Muhua and Chongping—long abolished.
idiomatic: Originally Bohai Anyuan Prefecture; two former counties—Muhua, Chongping—long abolished.
200 households.
Under Lu Prefecture.
Two hundred li to the northwest.

literal: Xian Prefecture, Fengxian Army, upper, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Xian Prefecture (Fengxian Army, upper rank), military commissioner.
Originally Bohai Xiande Prefecture territory.

literal: Shizong established it to tend the Xian Mausoleum.
idiomatic: Shizong founded it to serve the Xian Mausoleum.

literal: The Xian Mausoleum is the Renhuang King's tomb.
idiomatic: Xian Mausoleum is the tomb of the Renhuang King.

literal: The Renhuang King loved reading and disliked hunting; he bought tens of thousands of scrolls and built a hall called Wanghai on the summit of Mount Yiwulü.
idiomatic: Renhuang King favored books over the chase, bought tens of thousands of scrolls, and built Wanghai Hall atop Mount Yiwulü.

literal: South of the mountain to the sea is one hundred thirty li.
idiomatic: One hundred thirty li from the mountain's south face to the sea.

literal: In Datong year 1 Shizong personally escorted the Renhuang King's coffin returning from Bianjing.
idiomatic: Datong year 1: Shizong personally escorted the Renhuang King's coffin back from Bianjing.

literal: Because the Renhuang King loved Yiwulü's strange peaks and fine waters, he was buried there.
idiomatic: Renhuang King loved Yiwulü's landscape, so he was buried there.

literal: The mountain form folds in six layers; within it a shadow hall was built, magnificent in scale.
idiomatic: Sixfold mountain folds enclosed a shadow hall of magnificent scale.

literal: The prefecture lay southeast of the mountain; more than three hundred Eastern Capital households were moved to fill it.
idiomatic: The prefecture stood southeast of the mountain; over three hundred Eastern Capital households were settled there.

literal: In Yingli year 1 Muzong buried Shizong on the western hill of Xian Mausoleum and forbade fuel gathering.
idiomatic: Yingli year 1: Muzong buried Shizong on Xian Mausoleum's western hill and banned woodcutting.

literal: There were Thirteen Mountains and the Sha River.
idiomatic: Thirteen Mountains and the Sha River lay within it.

literal: Subordinate to Changning and Jiqing two palaces; military affairs belonged to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.
idiomatic: Under Changning and Jiqing palaces; military affairs to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.

literal: Governing three prefectures and three counties:
idiomatic: Three prefectures, three counties:
Fengxian County.

literal: Originally Han Wulü County—that is Yiwulü, Youzhou's guardian mountain.
idiomatic: Originally Han Wulü County—Mount Yiwulü, guardian peak of Youzhou.

literal: Shizong carved out Liaodong Changle County people as tomb households, subordinate to Changning Palace.
idiomatic: Shizong took Liaodong Changle households as tomb keepers under Changning Palace.
Shandong County.
It was formerly Han Wangping County.

literal: Muzong cut Bohai Yongfeng County people as tomb households, subordinate to Jiqing Palace.
idiomatic: Muzong assigned Bohai Yongfeng households as tomb keepers under Jiqing Palace.
Guiyi County.

literal: When Xian Prefecture was first established Bohai people came voluntarily to labor; Shizong commiserated and registered their households as a county, subordinate to Changning Palace.
idiomatic: At Xian Prefecture's founding Bohai people volunteered labor; Shizong registered them as Guiyi County under Changning Palace.

literal: Jia Prefecture, Jiaping Army, lower, cishi.
idiomatic: Jia Prefecture (Jiaping Army, lower), cishi.
Under Xian Prefecture.

literal: Liaoxi Prefecture, Fucheng Army, middle, cishi.
idiomatic: Liaoxi Prefecture (Fucheng Army, middle rank), cishi.

literal: Originally Han Liaoxi Commandery land; Shizong established the prefecture, subordinate to Changning Palace, belonging to Xian Prefecture.
idiomatic: Originally Han Liaoxi Commandery; Shizong founded the prefecture under Changning Palace within Xian Prefecture.
One county:
Changqing County.

literal: In Tonghe year 8 established with people from various palace intendant offices.
idiomatic: Tonghe year 8: founded with households from palace intendant offices.
Kang Prefecture (lower rank), cishi.

literal: Shizong moved Bohai Suibin Prefecture households to establish it, belonging to Xian Prefecture.
idiomatic: Shizong settled Suibin Prefecture Bohai households here under Xian Prefecture.

literal: At first subordinate to Changning Palace; later to Jiqing Palace.
idiomatic: First under Changning Palace; later under Jiqing Palace.
One county:
Suibin County.
Originally Bohai Suibin Prefecture territory.
Zong Prefecture (lower rank), cishi.

literal: At Shixiong Mountain in Liaodong; Yelü Longyun settled captured Han people there.
idiomatic: On Liaodong's Shixiong Mountain Yelü Longyun settled Han captives.

literal: Shengzong established it as a prefecture, subordinate to the Wenzhong Princely House.
idiomatic: Shengzong raised it to a prefecture under the Wenzhong princely house.

literal: When the prince died it belonged to the Intendant Office.
idiomatic: After the prince's death it passed to the Intendant Office.
One county:
Xiongshan County.
Originally Bohai county territory.

literal: Qian Prefecture, Guangde Army, upper, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Qian Prefecture (Guangde Army, upper), military commissioner.
Originally Han Wulü County territory.

literal: Shengzong Tonghe year 3 established 13 to tend Jingzong's Qian Mausoleum.
idiomatic: Shengzong Tonghe year 3 founded it thirteenth note: to serve Jingzong's Qian Mausoleum.
It held the Ningshen Hall.

literal: Subordinate to Chongde Palace; military affairs belonged to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.
idiomatic: Under Chongde Palace; military affairs to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.
